thread:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: multiple GPU host reboots and PCIe AERs observed in us-central1 inference cluster (pool: gen2-infer). Severity: P1. Impact: 15% of requests experiencing increased latency/errors. Please ack and follow runbook.
ryan_oncall: ack. jumping in. grabbing current status and toasts. Who's seeing the reboots in metrics?
maya_sre: I'm seeing node restarts (host reboot) spikes starting ~1933332440 in monitoring. Kernel OOPS + AER logs correlate. Some nodes show ECC corrected error counts climbing.
jon_runtime: From the serving side: traffic for gen2-infer had retries and timeouts to fallback models ~5m ago. We auto-failed over some requests but saw increased tail latency. Rolling deploy was not in flight.
chi_infra: I'm pulling provider instance events now. Saw unexpected host reset events for three instances in the same AZ. Opening provider ticket but need logs first.
ryan_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) drain any nodes with recent reboots 2) migrate live replicas off affected hosts 3) increase retries + extend timeouts temporarily 4) contact provider. who's on logs?
maya_sre: I'm collecting dmesg and nvidia-smi logs. saving to /tmp/incident-1933333000/.
jon_runtime: I'll flip traffic routing to avoid the affected host pool. Also enabling additional caching to reduce token generation pressure.
amy_csm: Heads up — one large customer (acme-analytics) reported increased 5xxs. I'm drafting a customer update with ETA for mitigation.
ryan_oncall: paste relevant logs here. include dmesg and nvml dumps.
maya_sre: ```
[  123.456789] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: severity=Corrected, type=Data Link Layer, id=0000
[  123.456792] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: GPU ECC error: device memory corrected errors: 42
[  124.001234] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: OOPS in nv-host-driver
``` 
maya_sre: also nvml sample (truncated): ```
GPU 0: ecc_corrected_cnt=42, ecc_uncorrected_cnt=0, temp=78C, power=250W
GPU 1: ecc_corrected_cnt=39, ecc_uncorrected_cnt=0, temp=81C
``` 
chi_infra: Provider console events: "Host reboot initiated by hypervisor due to PCIe error" for instances: gen2-infer-12, gen2-infer-18, gen2-infer-21. All in us-central1-a.
ryan_oncall: hypothesis list: 1) noisy neighbor causing PCIe errors and thermal stress 2) hardware degradation on host (slot/controller) 3) recent infra kernel driver regression 4) cloud host hypervisor bug. Rank by likelihood 1->4.
jon_runtime: adding symptom: KV cache miss storms coincided with time window — could be workload spike exposing marginal hardware.
maya_sre: adding evidence: ECC corrected counts steadily increase then host reboots. No uncorrected ECCs recorded. dmesg shows repeated AER notices minutes before OOPS.
leah_prod: is this hitting dedicated customers? We have one dedicated pool that runs in same AZ but different host type — so likely unaffected. Confirmed: dedicated pools OK.
amy_csm: Sending customer note to acme with current mitigations and invite to private channel if they want real-time updates.
chi_infra: Provider asked for full host logs and stack traces. I'm assembling kernel dump files, vmcore, and driver logs. ETA 20m.
ryan_oncall: short-term: continue draining/replacing affected nodes and scale up unaffected pools to absorb load. jon, can you add temporary routing rule to prefer us-west1 for new requests? We want to reduce blast radius.
jon_runtime: On it. Adding routing weight shift + warm-up new nodes. Will update when traffic ramps.
maya_sre: note: one node once rebooted came back but nvml shows fewer GPUs detected for ~10 minutes, then full topology restored. Suggest checking GPU firmware versions too.
ryan_oncall: action items so far: - chi: send compiled logs to provider & severity escalation - maya: collect full vmcore + gdb traces and upload to s3 (path) - jon: shift routing + increase retries - amy: customer comms - me: continue timeline and RCA thread.
maya_sre: uploaded archives: s3://redwood-incidents/1933333000/dmesg.tar.gz and s3://redwood-incidents/1933333000/nvml-dumps.tar.gz
chi_infra: provider ticket #PV-115762 opened. I'll paste link once available.
jon_runtime: routing change deployed. preferring us-west and scaling gen2-infer pool by 30% in unaffected regions.
amy_csm: sent customer note to acme-analytics, included temporary mitigation and SLA impact estimate. Awaiting reply.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations in progress. status: traffic shifted, affected hosts drained, provider escalated. next update in 30m or on major change.
ryan_oncall: collecting timeline so far: 1933332440 first AERs seen in monitoring -> 1933332503 first host reboot -> 1933332580 retries/fallbacks spike -> 1933332660 acme reports errors -> 1933333000 on-call paged -> mitigations kicked off.
maya_sre: early hypothesis lean: hardware/PCIe link degradation amplified by workload burst — leads to corrected ECC storms then kernel/driver OOPS and host reset. Need provider validation of host hardware and firmware logs.
chi_infra: provider responded: "We see repeated AERs and have scheduled a host replacement and hypervisor trace analysis. Please provide vmcore." They gave provisional ticket link: https://provider.example.com/ticket/PV-115762
jon_runtime: note for RCA: collect model-run-length distributions and token-per-request during window, plus batch size changes. Could be workload pattern stress test.
amy_csm: acme replied: "Thanks for the update. We'll monitor. Please ping when RCA ready." Marking customer as engaged.
ryan_oncall: plan for next 2 hours: continue host replacements, collect full traces, confirm whether firmware/drivers need patching, and produce initial RCA draft. If provider confirms hardware fault, plan replacement and migration for any remaining workloads in that AZ.
maya_sre: will start building timeline doc and attach log snippets. I'll ping once initial RCA draft uploaded to confluence.
jon_runtime: disabling aggressive prefetch and reducing concurrency on spill-prone models as precaution.
leah_prod: also flagging this for infra change: add PCIe AER monitoring alert earlier and ECC rate thresholds to preempt reboots.
ryan_oncall: thanks everyone. keep updates here. If we see new host reboots, tag me @ryan_oncall and escalate immediately.
incident-bot: Incident severity unchanged. All participants please update thread when actions complete."
